name: Electric Assisted Bicycle
description: A bicycle with two or three wheels, a seat or saddle, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts. From December 1, 2026 it falls in one of three classes: class 1 pedal assist and class 2 throttle, both to 20 mph, and class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph; until then its motor alone may not push it past 20 mph.

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels, a seat or saddle, fully operable pedals and a motor of no more than 750 watts (N.C. Gen. Stat. §20-4.01(7a))
Its top speed on motor power alone on level ground is 20 mph (N.C. Gen. Stat. §20-4.01(7a))

Class 1 assists only while the rider is pedaling and class 2 can propel it without pedaling, both to 20 mph; class 3 assists only while pedaling, to 28 mph (N.C. Gen. Stat. §20-4.01(7a), as amended by Session Law 2026-46)
Riders and passengers under 18 on a class 3 must wear a helmet meeting federal safety standards (N.C. Gen. Stat. §20-171.3, enacted by Session Law 2026-46)
Not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration or insurance (N.C. Gen. Stat. §20-4.01(23))
The rider has the duties of a vehicle driver under the traffic laws

It may be ridden on all roadways, bicycle lanes and multiuse paths, except where a city or county restricts it, or the Department of Natural and Cultural Resources does in state parks and historic sites (N.C. Gen. Stat. §20-171.3, enacted by Session Law 2026-46)
Cities and counties may restrict classes and set speed limits on multiuse paths and sidewalks, and may require helmets for riders and passengers under 18 on class 1 and class 2 (Session Law 2026-46)
One that exceeds these limits falls under moped rules, which require registration, insurance, a helmet and a rider 16 or older
